newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Foreign shareholding limit in Air NZ set at 49 pct.
newsitem.headline: Foreign shareholding limit in Air NZ set at 49 pct.

text.p: The New Zealand government on Monday said it had approved an application by Air New Zealand to lift the limits on foreign shareholding in the national flag carrier to 49 percent from 35 percent.
But it would retain the restriction on aggregate foreign airline holdings in the company at 35 percent. Individual foreign airlines would be allowed to hold up to 25 percent.

Shareholding Minister Doug Kidd said the decision, made under the provisions of the so-called "Kiwi share", was a logical consequence of negotiations over a single trans-Tasman aviation market and harmonised New Zealand's foreign shareholding restrictions with those adopted by Australia at the time of the Qantas Airways float last year.
He said the change did not require a change in government policy but reflected the emerging international position.

He said the kiwi share, established when the government privatised the airline in 1989, was a mechanism to ensure Air New Zealand could operate under air services agreements negotiated by the government.
He said the extra capital required by Air New Zealand to expand was "simply not available in New Zealand".
The announcement coincided with Air NZ's publication of the terms of its planned purchase of half of Australia's Ansett Holdings from TNT Ltd.
Air NZ is 19.9 percent owned by Qantas and 42.5 percent by Brierley Investments Ltd
